skill.name: backend-queries
skill.description: Write secure, performant, and optimized database queries using parameterized queries, eager loading, proper indexing, and transaction management. Use this skill when writing database queries in controllers, repositories, services, or model methods, when using query builders or ORM methods, when implementing filtering/sorting/pagination logic, when optimizing N+1 query problems with eager loading, when working with joins and complex queries, when implementing query caching, or when wrapping related operations in database transactions.
skill.summary: Guide backend query work with secure parameters, eager loading, indexes, caching, and transactions.
skill.author: DevanB

remediation.suggestion: Move the referenced guidance into the skill package or replace the parent-directory link with inline instructions.

content.value_statement: Backend query code often becomes slow, unsafe, or hard to maintain. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward safer parameters, eager loading, indexes, caching, and transactions.
actual_capabilities: Guides use of parameterized queries for raw SQL and query builders.
Prompts eager loading to reduce N+1 query problems.
Encourages selecting needed columns instead of broad SELECT usage.
Supports filtering, sorting, pagination, joins, subqueries, and aggregations.
Covers database indexes, query caching, query timeouts, and transaction boundaries.
limitations: Depends on an external parent-directory standards file for full instructions.
Does not include database-specific syntax examples in the packaged file.
Does not run benchmarks, migrations, or automated query analysis.
Requires project context to choose exact indexes or transaction scope.

use_cases.title: Secure Repository Queries
use_cases.description: Create repository methods that use parameterized filters and avoid unsafe raw SQL handling.

use_cases.title: Reduce Slow ORM Access
use_cases.description: Review controllers and services for N+1 query patterns and missing eager loading.

use_cases.title: Plan Query Performance Work
use_cases.description: Identify useful indexes, timeouts, caching points, and pagination boundaries before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Query
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this backend query for security, performance, and maintainability. Check parameters, selected columns, eager loading, and pagination.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one controller, service, or repository method.

prompt_templates.title: Fix N Plus One Access
prompt_templates.prompt: Find N+1 query risks in this code path. Recommend eager loading or query restructuring that preserves the existing response shape.
prompt_templates.scenario: Improving ORM usage without changing product behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Design Filtering and Pagination
prompt_templates.prompt: Design safe filtering, sorting, and pagination for this endpoint. Include validation rules, parameterized query patterns, and index considerations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Building a new list endpoint or search endpoint.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Transactional Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this multi-step database workflow. Propose transaction boundaries, timeout handling, cache invalidation, and query optimizations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of related writes and reads.

output_examples.input: Review a user search endpoint that concatenates filters and returns every user column.
output_examples.output: The review flags unsafe filter handling, excessive column selection, and missing pagination limits. It recommends parameter binding, explicit fields, validated sort options, and index checks.

output_examples.input: Optimize an order details view that loads each line item and product separately.
output_examples.output: The output identifies an N+1 pattern and suggests eager loading related records. It also notes where caching may help repeated reads.

output_examples.input: Plan a checkout workflow with inventory updates and payment records.
output_examples.output: The response outlines transaction boundaries, rollback points, timeout handling, and consistency checks for related database operations.

best_practices: Provide the relevant model, table, endpoint, and expected data volume.
Ask for both security and performance review when raw SQL is present.
Confirm suggested indexes and cache rules against real query plans.
anti_patterns: Do not paste secrets, credentials, or production connection strings.
Do not request broad rewrites without sharing current query behavior.
Do not accept index suggestions without checking write impact and storage cost.

faq.question: What does this skill help improve?
faq.answer: It helps improve backend database query safety, performance, and maintainability.

faq.question: Does it support raw SQL?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill explicitly calls for parameterization when raw queries or complex SQL are used.

faq.question: Can it solve N+1 query issues?
faq.answer: It can guide detection and fixes through eager loading or query restructuring.

faq.question: Does it create database indexes automatically?
faq.answer: No. It can recommend index considerations, but implementation needs project and database review.

faq.question: Is the packaged skill self-contained?
faq.answer: No. The reviewed file points to a parent-directory standards file for detailed guidance.

faq.question: Which AI tools does it support?
faq.answer: The metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
